The two quadrilaterals shown above are similar. What is the correct similarity statement?
question.worked_solution:
First, let's find the measures of unknown angles. Since the sum of the measures of internal angles of a quadrilateral is ${360}^{∘},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠R+m∠T+m∠U+m∠V & ={360}^{∘} \\ m∠R+{130}^{∘}+{50}^{∘}+{110}^{∘} & ={360}^{∘} \\ m∠R+{290}^{∘} & ={360}^{∘} \\ m∠R & ={70}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly,

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠O+m∠N+m∠Q+m∠P & ={360}^{∘} \\ {70}^{∘}+{130}^{∘}+m∠Q+{110}^{∘} & ={360}^{∘} \\ m∠Q+{310}^{∘} & ={360}^{∘} \\ m∠Q & ={50}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the quadrilaterals are similar, and

$$
\begin{aligned}∠R≅∠O,\,∠T≅∠N,\,∠U≅∠Q,\,∠V≅∠P.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that 

- $R$ corresponds to $O,$

- $T$ corresponds to $N,$

- $U$ corresponds to $Q,$

- $V$ corresponds to $P.$

Therefore, $RTUV∼ONQP.$
